purpose: Primary-source verification gate for species-resolved evidence before public evidence_detail surfacing. QA/schema success is not source-truth verification.
rules: Only records with status verified_primary may be promoted as named supporting records in public evidence_detail.
A verified occurrence or husbandry diet record is descriptive evidence, not a safety trial or feeding prescription.
Related Testudo evidence must remain related-taxon evidence and must not be relabeled as exact Testudo graeca ibera evidence.
Genus-level exact-Ibera observations must not be rewritten as exact plant species.
Unverified records remain excluded from public named-record surfacing until the underlying source is checked.
A stored species-evidence claim that conflicts with the checked primary table is hold_source_conflict and must not be surfaced publicly.
When a source-conflict audit establishes that a stored claim is unsupported by the checked primary table, remove the claim from the evidence asset rather than preserving it as evidence.

records.verification: AJVR 73(11):1781-1786 explicitly states the Hermann's tortoise study diet included ribwort plantain (Plantago lanceolata).
records.scope: related Testudo husbandry/study diet; not a plant safety trial

records.verification: ZooNotes 228 results explicitly list Plantago lanceolata among plants consumed by wild Testudo hermanni.
ZooNotes 228 explicitly reports Trifolium sp., including Trifolium campestre, for Testudo hermanni.
records.scope: related Testudo direct wild observation; not Ibera Trifolium species evidence

records.verification: Herpetologica 67(3) Table 1 lists Trifolium sp., leaves, in wild Testudo hermanni hermanni fecal diet data.
records.scope: related Testudo wild fecal evidence; genus only

records.verification: Soler, Martinez-Silvestre & Roca 2012 Table I lists Trifolium campestre seeds, 2 remains (0.56%), from Garraf Testudo hermanni fecal samples.
records.scope: related Testudo wild fecal evidence; exact plant species

records.verification: The paper's husbandry section explicitly includes Trifolium repens in the usual native wild-plant diet.
records.scope: related Testudo semi-natural husbandry context; not a controlled safety trial

records.verification: Soler, Martinez-Silvestre & Roca 2012 Table I lists Medicago sativa fruit remains, 2 remains (0.56%), in Garraf Testudo hermanni feces.
records.scope: related Testudo wild fecal evidence; exact plant species

records.verification: The same Table I separately lists Medicago truncatula, M. minima var. recta, and M. secundiflora remains.
records.scope: related Testudo species-resolution context; does not establish species interchangeability

records.verification: Herpetologica 67(3) Table 1 lists Medicago lupulina leaves in wild Testudo hermanni hermanni diet samples.
The paper's husbandry section explicitly includes Sonchus oleraceus in the usual native wild-plant diet.
records.scope: related Testudo semi-natural husbandry context; not a controlled safety trial

records.verification: Franch & Oller, Serra Balmeta field study (summer 1998; manuscript dated 25 Jan 1999) reports three Testudo hermanni hermanni individuals captured while feeding and explicitly names Plantago lanceolata among the consumed plants.
records.scope: related Testudo direct field feeding observation; small descriptive observation, not a safety trial or frequency prescription
records.source: Franch M, Oller M. Estudi d'una població de tortuga mediterrània (Testudo hermanni hermanni) a la Serra Balmeta (Albera). Field period 13 Jul-21 Sep 1998; manuscript 25 Jan 1999.

records.verification: Chelonian Conservation and Biology 2(1):36-42 Table 1 explicitly lists Sonchus oleraceus among wild food plants in the Souss Valley T. g. graeca diet.
records.scope: related T. g. graeca field diet record; not exact Ibera or a safety trial
records.source: Bayley JR, Highfield AC. 1996. Chelonian Conservation and Biology 2(1):36-42.

records.verification: Muñoz, Soler & Martínez-Silvestre 2009 Table 1 identifies Medicago sativa remains (fruit, leaves and stems) in Testudo hermanni hermanni fecal samples from Montsant. The Montsant reintroduction report also lists M. sativa leaves among consumed plants.
records.scope: related Testudo wild/reintroduced-population fecal diet evidence; exact plant species, not exact Ibera or a safety trial
records.source: Muñoz A, Soler J, Martínez-Silvestre A. 2009. Aportaciones al estudio de la alimentación de Testudo hermanni hermanni en el Parque Natural de la Sierra de Montsant. Bol. Asoc. Herpetol. Esp. 20:54-56.
